intro: Search for palestinian olive oil from Malaysia and two very different bottles come back: one names a place on the front, the other admits in small print that it blends oils from more than one country. That gap is the subject here.

Arabian Village is Palestinian cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil, distributed in Malaysia by Berkat Madinah Store. Single origin is not decoration on that label — it is a claim narrow enough to be checked.

sections.heading: What makes Palestinian olive oil different?

blocks.text: Palestinian olive oil comes from a narrow band of hill country with hot dry summers, wet winters, thin limestone soil and groves set along stone terraces. Most groves are rain-fed rather than irrigated, the fruit is hand-picked in autumn, and the olives are pressed close to where they grew.
No single element there is unique. The combination is, and so is a harvest that has stayed a village event rather than an industrial one.

sections.heading: Which olive varieties grow in Palestinian groves?

blocks.text: The dominant variety is the Nabali olive, often called Baladi, meaning local. Nabali Muhassan and Souri grow alongside it, and older Rumi trees appear in places. Nabali fruit gives an oil that reads green rather than sweet: grassy, faintly bitter, peppery in the throat.

items: Aroma — cut grass and green leaf, sometimes tomato leaf
Palate — green and lightly bitter, not buttery or nutty
Finish — peppery in the throat, strongest in a recent harvest
Colour — green-gold, deeper when the fruit was picked earlier

sections.heading: When is the Palestinian olive harvest?

blocks.text: The Palestinian olive harvest falls in autumn, broadly October into November, shifting with altitude and with how the rains came that year. It is short and it is social: families and neighbours working the same terraces. Fruit picked early gives greener, more bitter oil; fruit left longer, milder.
A harvest date therefore says more than a best-before date, which the bottler sets. It records when the fruit left the tree.

sections.heading: Why does single origin matter more than a blend?

blocks.text: Single origin means every olive in the bottle came from one defined place. A blend combines oil from several countries — legal, ordinary, and why the back label often reads as a list. The difference is not quality by decree; it is how much you can check.

sections.heading: What does the land itself do to the oil?

blocks.text: Rain-fed groves on terraced slopes carry less fruit per tree than irrigated orchards on flat ground, and the olives run smaller. The terraces exist because the hillsides are steep and the soil shallow; their walls hold what winter rain arrives. The trees then pass a dry summer unwatered.
Small plots and hand picking mean modest volumes and a short pressing window, so the oil is made in batches. Our [single-origin sourcing](/why-us) page covers the supply side.

sections.heading: How do you buy Palestinian olive oil in Malaysia?

blocks.text: In Malaysia, Arabian Village is distributed by Berkat Madinah Store, which opened in 2010. The oil is sold at its two branches, Ampang Jaya and Batu Caves, the larger, and through Berkat Madinah's own Shopee storefront and TikTok Shop — the same seller, not resellers.

conclusion.heading: Origin is a claim you can test

blocks.text: Single origin earns attention for a plain reason: it can be falsified. One region, one harvest window, one importer to question. Ask where the fruit grew, when it was picked and who imported it — then [compare the bottles and sizes](/shop).

faqs.a: Olive oil pressed from olives grown in Palestinian groves — largely rain-fed plantings on terraced hill country, picked in autumn and pressed nearby. Extra virgin means the oil was produced by mechanical means alone, without heat or solvents, and met the limits set for that grade.

faqs.q: What does Nabali olive oil taste like?
faqs.a: Green rather than sweet. Expect cut grass and green leaf on the nose, a light bitterness across the palate, and a peppery catch at the back of the throat. The pepper is sharpest in oil from a recent harvest and softens as a bottle ages.

faqs.q: When is the olive harvest in Palestine?
faqs.a: Autumn — broadly October into November, moving with altitude and with the year's rainfall. The window is short. Picking early yields greener, more bitter, more peppery oil; leaving the fruit on the tree longer yields a milder, rounder oil from the same trees.

faqs.q: Is single origin olive oil better than a blend?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Single origin describes where the olives came from, not how carefully the oil was made. What it gives you is something to check: one region, one harvest season, one importer to ask. A blend of several countries offers fewer facts to hold anyone to.

faqs.q: Where can I buy Palestinian olive oil in Malaysia?
faqs.a: Arabian Village is distributed by Berkat Madinah Store, in business since 2010. Buy it at the Ampang Jaya and Batu Caves branches, Batu Caves being the larger, or online through Berkat Madinah's own Shopee storefront and TikTok Shop. Those channels are the same shop.

faqs.a: RM59.00 for the 250 ml bottle and RM103.00 for the 500 ml. Price follows the size and not the flavour, so a bottle from the infused range costs the same as the classic oil at the same volume. Sizes are listed on the [shop page](/shop).
